To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present a novel data driven framework for semi-supervised learning, where the graph is learned using problem instances coming from a problem domain.
we present a data driven approach for semi-supervised learning that learns graph hyperparameters and provides formal performance guarantees.

we present a novel data driven algorithmic approach for designing semi supervised learning algorithms that can be provably shown to perform well in the online and distributional settings for large classes of domains, and that this approach can be applied to a wide range of graph based algorithms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: 1. What is the best way to create the graph for semi-supervised learning?
the problem of designing semi-supervised machine learning algorithms that can learn with only a few labeled examples, and can be applied to a variety of different problems and domains.

the following question: how can we leverage the problem instances coming from a problem domain to learn a semi-supervised learning algorithm that will perform well on new problem instances from the same problem domain? We believe that the techniques we develop in this thesis will have an important impact on the practical usefulness of semi-supervised learning methods, and more broadly on the field of data driven algorithms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we propose a novel data driven semi-supervised algorithm for learning graphs that provably performs well on new unseen instances.
we present a principled and data driven way for learning the hyperparameters for graph-based semi-supervision.
we provide a principled data-driven approach to graph-based semi-supervision.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present the first general principles for learning the graph in graph-based semi-supervision, and show how to learn a graph that is guaranteed to perform well for a large class of problems.

we provide a principled way for designing graph-based semi-supervise learning algorithms, which can learn from the data and generalize to new instances, and we also show how to leverage this to learn the hyperparameters for commonly-used parametric families of graph.
for a large class of problems, our algorithms provably learn to use the unlabeled data effectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the graph hyperparameters of semi-supervised learning methods can be learned from data, and this leads to algorithms that are provably more powerful and practical than the ones based on heuristic choices of hyperparameters.
it is possible to learn the graph in a principled manner and to provide strong theoretical guarantees for semi-supervised learning, even with only a small amount of supervision.
we can learn the graph hyperparameter from the data, which can be used in conjunction with any graph based semi-supervised learning algorithm to improve its performance.
